title: Modernize fallback orchestration and region routing sanitization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the smart routing layer to decouple fallback orchestration from policy evaluation, sanitize regional routing mappings, and upgrade routing dependencies (protobuf and grpc). Goal is to reduce contention on global locks, simplify policy adapters, and provide a compact fallback executor that is observable and testable. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, rollout, and post-rollout monitoring for the change.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluation and fallback orchestration are separate processes with a documented, stable interface
Fallback executor handles retries, backoff, and circuit-breaking without acquiring global routing locks
Regional routing mapping table is normalized and compacted, removing legacy shard aliases
End-to-end latency for small requests improves by >= 8% in stress tests and p99 latency does not regress
All internal and external API behavior unchanged (backwards-compatible), with feature flag to toggle new execution path
Migration runbook exists and tested on staging, with automatic rollback path in case of errors
tasks: Design public interface between policy-evaluator and fallback-executor (interface doc in Confluence)
Implement lock-free fallback queue and admission controller in routing runtime
Normalize regional routing table and remove obsolete aliases in mapping service
Upgrade protobuf to 3.21.x and grpc to 1.57.x, update generated stubs and CI containers
Add unit and integration tests that simulate cross-region failover and race conditions
Add telemetry: fallback decision traces, queue depth histograms, per-region admission rates
Prepare rollout plan with staged canary (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) and automated performance gates
Create migration runbook and DB migration script for mapping table compaction
notes: Trade-offs: introducing a lightweight message-passing layer between evaluator and executor increases code paths but reduces lock contention; acceptable because it simplifies metrics and failure isolation.
We considered a full rewrite of routing mapping service but scoped to compaction + alias removal to reduce rollout risk.
Protobuf/grpc upgrade required minor wire-compat checks; compatibility tests added in CI to prevent accidental proto breaking changes.
